last_outcome: M1-19 (iteration 33): FlightMap.tsx now tracks the segments/viewport it last settled at in a ref (restingViewRef), comparing viewport by value (width/height, not object reference - flight-demo.tsx constructs a fresh {width,height} literal on every useWindowDimensions() re-render) and segments by reference (safe since FlightScreen memoizes it on the route and viewport dimensions). Whenever either genuinely changes, pan resets to {x:0,y:0} and zoom resets to MIN_ZOOM - the resting fit-to-bounds view - rather than keep applying a stale gesture offset on top of newly-fit coordinates. Four new [M1-19] tests: a viewport-rotation-after-pan reset, a new-route-reference-after-pinch-and-pan reset (both zoom and pan), a maxZoom-only-rerender regression proving the M1-17 re-clamp scenario is unaffected, and (added after self-review) a mid-gesture viewport-change regression. Self-review (/code-review --effort high) found a real gap: the reset cleared pan/zoom state but never invalidated gestureStartRef, so a gesture still in progress (finger down, no release/terminate) would have its next move re-add the pre-change start.pan on top of the just-reset view - reproduced directly, then fixed by nulling gestureStartRef in the same reconciliation branch. pnpm run verify green throughout: 216 tests (floor 215->216), gate:roadmap ok (27 done/7 pending), gate:tests ok. No supabase/auth/RLS touched, no /security-review needed.
